# Mergiato

> Mergiato is a free desktop app for GitHub pull requests, the ones you ship and the ones you review (macOS today, Apple silicon and Intel). It puts your PR inbox, CI checks, stacked PRs, diffs of any size, code review threads, Vercel previews and the merge button in one window. It signs in through the user's own GitHub CLI (`gh`), so there are no access tokens to create, no GitHub App to install in the organization, no servers, no account and no analytics.

- Platform: macOS, one universal download for Apple silicon and Intel Macs. More platforms are coming.
- Price: free during the beta, every feature included. Paid plans, if any, come later with fair notice.
- Requirements: the GitHub CLI, signed in (`gh auth login`). Optional: the Vercel CLI, for preview deployments. No local clone needed (only for the docked terminal).
- Download: under 10 MB, a universal .dmg from https://github.com/alex-parra/mergiato-pull-request-app/releases/latest
- Maker: Alex Parra (https://github.com/alex-parra). Feedback and bugs: https://github.com/alex-parra/mergiato-pull-request-app/issues

## Who it is for

Developers who review or ship many pull requests a day on GitHub, including teams that use Graphite stacks and its merge queue, GitHub Actions and Vercel. It works for one person on a team: everything you do lands on GitHub as usual, so teammates don't have to switch.

## Features

- Inbox: "My PRs" (in progress, merged) and "Reviews" (review requested, reviewed by you), refreshed every 30 seconds, with check and review state on every row. Open any PR by link, `owner/repo#123` or `#123`.
- Checks: each job's latest run, its state and time, grouped by workflow. Re-run failed jobs, all jobs, or one job, from the PR. Updates every 10 seconds while jobs run.
- Changes: every file GitHub has, up to 3,000, drawn only near the view so large diffs stay smooth. File tree or list, unified or split, syntax colors, Viewed marks that reset when a file changes, generated files and lockfiles folded, one commit at a time.
- Review: comment on a line or a range, reply, react, resolve, edit or delete your comments. Approve, approve with a comment, or request changes. Drafts kept per line. Edit the title, description (with PR templates and image or video uploads), reviewers (including teams), labels and assignees.
- Stacked PRs: Graphite stacks, GitHub's native stacks and plain branch chains, shown on every PR with up and down jumps.
- Merge: one button that follows the repository's rules: Graphite's merge queue (queues the stack), GitHub's merge queue, or the repository's allowed merge methods. Two clicks to merge; when blocked it says why (approvals, conflicts, failing checks, the PR below in the stack).
- PR state: convert to draft, mark ready for review, close, reopen.
- Previews: each Vercel project's deployment state and link; deploy the branch's latest commit or redeploy, from the PR.
- Terminal: shells docked under each PR, in its local clone, kept running per PR.
- Agent review (optional): start a Claude Code review docked under the PR.
- Everyday details: reopens where you left off, shows the last inbox at once on launch, keeps the open PR current without refreshing, handles going offline, optimistic updates that roll back if GitHub refuses, six themes (three dark, three light), keyboard shortcuts for everything (Cmd-/ lists them), quit asks twice, signed automatic updates.

## Security and privacy

Mergiato drives the user's own CLIs: `gh`, `git` and, optionally, `vercel`. Requests go from the Mac straight to GitHub (and Vercel) with the user's existing access. There is no GitHub App, no OAuth grant, no tokens stored by Mergiato, no Mergiato servers, no account and no analytics.

## Install

1. Download the .dmg, open it and drag Mergiato to Applications.
2. First open: the app is not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS asks once. Allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway. Updates don't ask again. Some company-managed Macs block unsigned apps entirely.
3. If needed, install and sign in to the GitHub CLI: `brew install gh`, then `gh auth login`.

## Compared with

- GitHub in a browser: the same pull requests, but in one window instead of separate tabs for the PR, files, Actions, previews, stacks and notifications.
- GitHub Desktop: a git client for commits and branches. Mergiato is for the pull request side; they work side by side.
- Graphite: a service with its own web app and CLI for stacked PRs. Mergiato needs no account, sits on top of GitHub, and shows Graphite's stacks and merge queue when a team uses them.

## Pages

- [Mergiato vs GitHub Desktop: PRs vs commits](https://mergiato.com/compare/github-desktop/): GitHub Desktop is a git client for commits and branches, and can't comment on PRs. Mergiato is for the pull request side: review, checks, stacks and merges.
- [Mergiato vs Graphite: which fits your GitHub PRs](https://mergiato.com/compare/graphite/): Graphite is a hosted service for stacked PRs, AI review and a merge queue. Mergiato is a free desktop app on your GitHub CLI that shows and merges its stacks.
- [Mergiato vs Pulldog: desktop apps for PRs](https://mergiato.com/compare/pulldog/): Pulldog is a Mac code review client for GitHub, GitLab and more. Mergiato covers the whole life of a GitHub PR: checks, stacks, merge queues, previews.
- [Review large GitHub pull requests, every file](https://mergiato.com/large-pull-requests/): GitHub hides big diffs behind Load diff, and its diff API stops at 300 files. Mergiato shows every file, up to 3,000, and draws a 914-file PR in 0.2 seconds.
- [Security and privacy: what Mergiato can access](https://mergiato.com/security/): Mergiato runs on your own GitHub CLI and sends every request straight from your machine to GitHub. Here's what it can access, and what it keeps.
- [Review and merge stacked PRs on GitHub](https://mergiato.com/stacked-prs/): See the whole stack on every PR, from Graphite, GitHub's own stacks or branch chains, and merge it the way your repo does, through Graphite's queue or GitHub's.
